text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"mkdir -p /tmp/exposed-alias-design-astra cat > /tmp/exposed-alias-design-astra/design.md <<'EOF' # Search provenance owned by the search result ## Problem `west mid` matches a funder alias but the result shows only `Unite Union`. The repository currently returns the maximum canonical/alias score, and every later layer loses its origin. Preserve canonical identity while carrying the winning source. Keep exact word_similarity scores, inclusive request strictness, independent entity limits, one result per funder, and existing MP/funder merge behavior. Add the three requested GiST indexes without claiming that ordinary function comparisons use them. ## Usage (caller's view) Repository caller: ```rust let funders: Vec<(FunderSearchMatch, SearchSimilarity)> = repo.get_funders_by_text_search_score(&request).await?; // Sorted, thresholded, limited funder identities; winning source travels with identity. ``` HTTP conversion: ```rust match entity { Entity::Funder(hit) => { // identity/name/kind from hit.funder(); matched_by from hit.matched_by() } Entity::ParliamentMember(member) => { // identity/name from member; matched_by = SearchMatchSource::Name } } ``` UI: ```svelte {entity.name} {#if entity.matchedBy.kind === "alias"} Matched alias: {entity.matchedBy.name} {/if} ``` Keep existing highlightName segments for both displayed names. Never use raw HTML. ## Shape Extend `domain/models/entity_search.rs`, the existing search domain, rather than changing `Funder` details or introducing another service. ```rust #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)] #[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")] pub enum SearchMatchSource { Name, Alias { name: String }, } #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct FunderSearchMatch { funder: Funder, matched_by: SearchMatchSource, } impl FunderSearchMatch { pub fn new(funder: Funder, matched_by: SearchMatchSource) -> Self { todo!() } pub fn funder(&self) -> &Funder { todo!() } pub fn matched_by(&self) -> &SearchMatchSource { todo!() } } pub enum Entity { Funder(FunderSearchMatch), ParliamentMember(ParliamentMember), } ``` `FunderSearchMatch` owns the association between the identity and its query-specific source. `SearchMatchSource` makes an alias payload compulsory. `Entity` prevents MPs from acquiring alias metadata. `Funder` remains reusable outside search. Existing Entity getters delegate through the funder hit. Replace `From<&Funder>` with `From<&FunderSearchMatch>`; do not retain a compatibility route that silently assigns Name. ParliamentMemberRepo retains its tuple return type and its ingestion callers are untouched. FunderRepo replaces only its tuple's first element. The merge function changes its funder input and otherwise preserves its two-pointer comparison, including the present alternating MP/funder behavior on equal scores. EntitySearchService still returns Vec. At the SQL boundary, `matched_alias: Option` is a storage representation; map None to Name and Some to Alias immediately. HTTP SearchEntity adds `matched_by: SearchMatchSource` using the canonical enum's serde encoding. No separately maintained string enum or response mapper for the source vocabulary. This concentrates query policy in the repository and exposes just the domain outcome, per boundary-discipline and minimize-reader-load. Wire examples: ```json {"id":"…","name":"Unite Union","kind":"Funder","funder_kind":"Trade Union","matched_by":{"kind":"alias","name":"West Midlands Unite"}} {"id":"123","name":"John Smith","kind":"MP","funder_kind":null,"matched_by":{"kind":"name"}} ``` Frontend uses `SearchMatchSource = {kind:"name"} | {kind:"alias"; name:string}`. Funder entities carry either source; MP entity matchedBy has the name-only subtype. Parse unknown JSON in the existing readEntities boundary, reject absent/unknown source kinds, missing/non-string alias name, and an alias source for MP. Update fixtures with the new required field in this change. Do not guess Name from missing metadata. The backend and frontend ship as one contract here. ## Query contract The smallest exact query replaces repeated correlated MAX calculations with one best-alias lateral subquery. Use sqlx::query! as today: ```sql SELECT f.id, f.funder_name AS name, f.funder_kind AS kind, GREATEST(n.score, COALESCE(a.score, 0::real)) AS similarity_score, CASE WHEN a.score > n.score THEN a.funder_alias END AS matched_alias FROM exposed.funders f CROSS JOIN LATERAL ( SELECT word_similarity($1, f.funder_name) AS score ) n LEFT JOIN LATERAL ( SELECT fa.funder_alias, word_similarity($1, fa.funder_alias) AS score FROM exposed.funder_aliases fa WHERE fa.funder_id = f.id ORDER BY score DESC, fa.funder_alias COLLATE "C" ASC LIMIT 1 ) a ON TRUE WHERE GREATEST(n.score, COALESCE(a.score, 0::real)) >= $2 ORDER BY similarity_score DESC, f.id ASC LIMIT $3 ``` Pass i64::from(req.max_entries()) as $3 and remove rank/take_while. Alias lexical ties have deterministic byte order. A strict `>` assigns equal canonical/alias scores to canonical. No aliases gives canonical. Zero threshold still returns zero-score rows; threshold one remains inclusive. LIMIT applies after one row per funder, so alias multiplicity cannot consume identity slots. Retain the exact score value and add deterministic identity ordering for same-score rows. Apply the corresponding `ORDER BY similarity_score DESC, parliament_member_id ASC LIMIT $3` cleanup to member SQL while keeping its tuple API. Three baseline indexes: ```sql CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS members_name_trgm_gist_idx ON exposed.members USING gist (name exposed.gist_trgm_ops); CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS funders_name_trgm_gist_idx ON exposed.funders USING gist (funder_name exposed.gist_trgm_ops); CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS funder_aliases_alias_trgm_gist_idx ON exposed.funder_aliases USING gist (funder_alias exposed.gist_trgm_ops); ``` Fold these into the sole baseline up migration, after their tables. Down table drops remove associated indexes; explicit drops are optional if following current down style. For live DB apply these idempotent statements only after inspecting existing definitions, then schema-verify before checksum repair per db/README.md. IF NOT EXISTS does not verify an existing index definition. ### Honest GiST applicability This exact aggregate query does not become index-backed merely because indexes exist. Function comparisons `word_similarity(...) >= $2` do not use GiST. The indexes support pg_trgm threshold operators and KNN word distance `column <->> query`. A read-only EXPLAIN of `SELECT ... FROM exposed.funder_aliases ORDER BY funder_alias <->> 'west mid' LIMIT 10` can establish the expected KNN access path on realistic data, but is not evidence that the application's grouped funder query uses it. Do not claim a runtime speedup. I recommend shipping requested indexes and provenance with this exact query. If the accepted task requires the application's search itself to exploit GiST, this candidate needs a deliberate second design decision before implementation. Changing all ranking to KNN distance can collapse distinct real scores through subtraction rounding; limiting alias rows before identity dedup can omit valid funders. Those are correctness costs, not harmless optimization details. Avoid a session threshold GUC entirely in this small change. ## Verification SQLx database tests should insert one funder with many matching aliases plus several distinct funders. Check identity limit is filled, each identity occurs once, source follows the highest score, original alias spelling survives, canonical wins equal scores, equal alias scores choose C lexical order, and strictness 0/1 plus an exact intermediate score are inclusive. Include a direct canonical match whose aliases score lower. Compare returned scores/IDs to a simple exhaustive reference query on the fixture. This catches candidate pruning errors more directly than an index-name assertion. Service tests must assert alias metadata survives mixed MP/funder ranking, including ties and empty sides. HTTP serialization test should assert the exact Name/Alias wire shapes. Frontend Playwright should consume an actual serialized fixture or matching golden shape, render canonical link with alias explanation, verify direct-name rows remain compact, preserve URL query/strictness navigation, reject malformed metadata, and display hostile alias markup literally. Check a long alias at a narrow viewport; wrap within the name column, avoid overflow, associate secondary text through aria-describedby on the canonical link if it sits outside the link. Keyboard focus remains one link per result. ## Tradeoffs accepted - We accept the existing funder scan in exchange for exact scoring and a small reviewable change. The three requested indexes are useful access paths, but not a claimed optimization of this grouped query. - We accept modifying search-only Entity's funder payload in exchange for making member-alias combinations impossible and preserving the service signature. - We accept a required additional JSON field in exchange for preventing old or malformed producers from falsely implying canonical matches. ## Alternatives considered A generic `SearchHit {entity:T,score,source}` used by both repositories would unify merge code, but changes ParliamentMemberRepo's ingestion consumers and permits aliases on MPs unless more type machinery is added. It hides scoring metadata while exposing an unnecessarily broad generic abstraction. A materialized search-name table with one canonical/alias row per identity would give one GiST search vocabulary and simplify future KNN retrieval. It introduces another state writer and invalidation rules on ingestion/loading, and still requires correct identity dedup before limit. Its broader ownership and mutation cost outweigh this read-only change. A transaction-local word_similarity_threshold plus index operators can prune candidates before exact filtering, but has strict/inclusive boundary and zero-threshold traps. It exposes connection-state policy in an otherwise simple search repository and needs more proof than this request warrants. ## Synthesis decision Pending parent arena comparison. Preserve the exact-score query and domain-owned source enum even if a better proven GiST query strategy is grafted in. ## Implementation reconciliation No implementation performed; source and AGENTS read in the designated task worktree. Artifact only is written. ## Open questions and risks Does the accepted user scope require demonstrated application-query GiST usage, or only the requested indexes? Parent can resolve from the original request without stopping for another user confirmation. If index usage is mandatory, reject this candidate's conservative query rather than report an optimization it does not supply. ## Next implementation step Introduce SearchMatchSource and FunderSearchMatch, update the repository return contract and SQL together, then carry the result through HTTP and frontend with the behavior tests above. EOF","max_output_tokens":1000}));

text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat >> /tmp/exposed-alias-design-astra/design.md <<'EOF'

### Late grounding evidence from parent

Parent verified read-only PostgreSQL 18 transaction-local threshold behavior: `<%` includes exact score 1 at threshold 1 and score 0 at threshold 0. This removes the hypothesized endpoint-exclusion concern for the observed database. A transaction-local operator prefilter can therefore be a practical index-backed alternative without an epsilon, provided each repository's query and `set_config(..., true)` share the same transaction and exact `>= $2` remains the final authority. Avoid deriving exact ranking from rounded KNN distance. Parent reproduced `west mid` at strictness 0.6 returning canonical `Unite the Union` through aliases at score 0.8888889.
EOF","max_output_tokens":200}));
